specPoints.text: understand how genetically modified plants can be used to improve food production

primer.text: Genetic modification lets breeders install whole new abilities into crop plants — insect-killing poisons from bacteria, herbicide tolerance, extra vitamins, drought tolerance. This note explains how those traits improve food production and weighs the field-level advantages against the ecological and economic worries.

lessons.title: Crops with Installed Abilities
lessons.opening: A GM plant carries foreign DNA chosen to improve food production. Bacterial genes let wheat and maize manufacture an insect-killing poison, other insertions tolerate herbicide sprays, golden rice makes vitamin A precursors, and drought-tolerant strains hold yields where water is scarce.
keyPoints: Genetic modification inserts foreign DNA into a plant's genome to add useful traits.
Wheat and maize carry a bacterial gene producing a poison that kills insect pests, raising yields.
Herbicide-resistant crops survive spraying that eliminates the weeds around them.
Golden rice carries plant and bacterial genes so its grains yield a chemical converted into vitamin A in the human body.
Drought-resistant GM crops grow better in very dry conditions and improve yields there.
Concerns include effects on wildflowers and insects, and human health questions not yet fully explored.

low.restatement: Borrow a gene from another organism, slip it into a crop, and the crop gains a new ability like pest-killing or drought-proofing.
low.analogy: Installing an app on a phone: the hardware stays, but new functions arrive from outside.
low.examPointer: Name at least two concrete GM examples — insect resistance and golden rice cover most mark schemes.

medium.restatement: GM crops are produced by inserting foreign genes conferring useful traits: bacterial poison genes protect wheat and maize from caterpillars and lift yields, herbicide tolerance lets sprays kill weeds without harming the crop, golden rice manufactures vitamin A precursors, and drought tolerance sustains yields in dry regions.
medium.analogy: Upgrading a fleet of vans with engines from a different maker so they run where the originals could not.
medium.examPointer: Pair every advantage with the production goal it serves — resistance, nutrition or yield — to show the food-production link.

check.stem: What does genetic modification actually do to a plant?

options.text: It inserts foreign DNA into the plant's genome to add new traits
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: It breeds the plant with a wild relative
options.explanation: Conventional crossing is not modification.

options.text: It sprays the plant with growth chemicals
options.explanation: Spraying changes conditions, not genes.

options.text: It radiates seeds to force mutations
options.explanation: Mutation breeding is a different technique.

check.stem: Which organism donated the insect-killing gene used in modified wheat and maize?

options.text: A bacterium
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: A caterpillar
options.explanation: The caterpillar is the pest being killed.

options.text: A fungus
options.explanation: Fungi are not the donor named.

options.text: The maize plant itself
options.explanation: The gene is foreign to the plant.

check.stem: How does herbicide-resistant crop technology protect yields?

options.text: Spraying kills the weeds around the crop while the crop itself survives
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: The spray fertilises the crop directly
options.explanation: Herbicides kill plants; they do not feed them.

options.text: The spray repels insect pests
options.explanation: Insects are not the target of herbicides.

options.text: The crop grows without any water
options.explanation: Resistance concerns chemicals, not drought.

check.stem: Why is golden rice significant for human nutrition?

options.text: Its grains produce a chemical the body converts into vitamin A
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: It cures malaria
options.explanation: Malaria is unrelated to rice engineering.

options.text: It grows without fertiliser
options.explanation: Nutrition, not fertiliser use, is the point.

options.text: It tastes sweeter than normal rice
options.explanation: Flavour is not the engineered trait.

check.stem: Which concern about GM crops relates to surrounding ecosystems?

options.text: Effects on wildflower and insect populations near the fields
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Rice grains becoming poisonous to birds
options.explanation: That specific claim is not taught.

options.text: Tractors using more diesel
options.explanation: Fuel use is not a GM concern.

options.text: Crops ripening too early
options.explanation: Ripening speed is not the worry cited.

check.stem: State what the term genetic modification means.
check.modelAnswer: Genetic modification means foreign DNA is added to an organism's genome so its traits change.

check.stem: Name the vitamin that golden rice helps humans produce.
check.modelAnswer: Golden rice grains carry a chemical that the human body converts into vitamin A.

check.stem: Explain why insect-resistant GM crops can raise yields.
check.modelAnswer: The crops manufacture their own poison against insect pests such as caterpillars, so less leaf tissue is eaten and the plants channel more growth into harvestable yield.

check.stem: A drought-prone region must choose between ordinary seed and drought-tolerant GM seed. Apply the evidence to advise.
check.modelAnswer: Choose the drought-tolerant GM seed, because engineered plants grow better in very dry conditions and hold yields where ordinary crops would fail.

glossary.definition: Inserting foreign DNA into an organism's genome to give it new traits.
A chemical that kills plants; resistant crops survive spraying that kills weeds.
Rice engineered with genes that make its grains produce vitamin A precursors.
